expected.projects: no additional Vercel project caller rules; accept only an empty serialized container until documented default-self serialization has been reviewed

trustedSources.enableVercelCiSameRepository_documented_: The official project API schema lists this boolean field but the official docs reviewed do not define its behavior. Expected false is a fail-closed source policy, not a claim about undocumented semantics.
trustedSources.projects_documented_semantics: Trusted Sources docs describe other Vercel projects added to this project as authorized callers; default same-project access is documented separately. No additional Vercel project callers are expected. If the API serializes default self-access as a project rule, its exact representation must be read and reviewed before accepting a parser exception.
trustedSources.validator_source_status: Current source requires explicit false for enableVercelCiSameRepository and an empty projects object/array; unknown, missing, or nonempty values fail closed.

required_effective_operations: Read the exact target project's identity, deployments, domains, aliases, and deployment file metadata required by the workflow
Create the reviewed staged Production deployment for the exact target project
Promote or restore a deployment only for the exact target project
credential.required_token_scope: Project scope for prj_QNMVdxTkPOad4ynN4fwFCYEST8Jk only; team scope and full-account scope are not acceptable.
credential.documented_project_scope_behavior: Vercel docs say a project-scoped token can only read and write resources belonging to that one project and denies requests to other projects, user-level resources, and team-level resources. Project scope is a resource boundary, not documented verb-level minimization.

documented_rbac_constraints.full_production_deployment: Current Extended Permissions docs describe CLI Production deployment, rollback, and promotion of any deployment; the permission is compatible with the Developer team role, already included in Owner/Member. The docs do not establish that this permission is limited to a single project's deployment actions.
documented_rbac_constraints.project_developer: Project-level role limited to assigned projects; docs describe project deployment and development/preview environment-variable management, but do not establish the exact CLI Production deployment, rollback, and promote/restore operation set required here.
documented_rbac_constraints.project_admin: Includes full control of the assigned project's settings and Production deployments; this is broader than the required action set.
documented_rbac_constraints.access_groups: Project role assignments only; docs say team roles cannot be overridden and effective role combinations retain the most permissive permissions.

credential.effective_permission_proof: UNKNOWN; no existing token or provider permission readback was available, and official docs reviewed do not prove a role/token combination that grants only the required target-project reads and Production deployment/promote/restore actions while denying all other project/team writes.
credential.acceptance_rule: Do not issue or accept a credential until owner evidence proves the token is project-scoped to the exact target and its effective permissions include only the required target-project reads and Production deployment/promote/restore actions. Project scope alone is insufficient proof of verb-level restrictions. Reject team/full-account scope and any unproven or extra project-settings, environment, variable, domain, or team write permissions. If Vercel cannot isolate or prove this minimum set, readiness remains blocked; do not broaden access for convenience.
